newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl breaks ground for new German chancellery.
newsitem.headline: Kohl breaks ground for new German chancellery.

text.p: Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Tuesday that Germany's new chancellery building in Berlin would "radiate a relaxed self-confidence" and be a dignified symbol of the reunited nation to the world.

Breaking ground for the new chancellery near the Reichstag parliament building, Kohl said the boxy modern structure would stand in an area representing all the "splendour and hubris, destruction and recommencement" of recent German history.

The 400 million mark complex, which may not be finished by the government's planned move from Bonn in mid-1999, will be H-shaped, with a large block in the middle for the chancellor and cabinet and long wings on either side for his staff.
"The design radiates a relaxed self-confidence," said Kohl, according to an advance text of his speech. "It unites modesty with dignity."

The new building overlooking a bend in the Spree River, will be Berlin's third chancellery in this century. Until the 1930s, chancellors used Bismarck's office in the nearby Wilhelmstrasse, close to where Hitler build his New Reich Chancellery which was destroyed in World War Two.
Commenting on its location near Germany's first and future parliament building, Kohl said: "The Reichstag was built under the Kaisers. It stands for democracy.
"It was destroyed after the end of the Weimar Republic, as democracy itself was destroyed. Its reconstruction after the war stood for the new beginning of a democratic state."

Nearby is also the Brandenburg Gate, which he said was "like no other building in the world the symbol of the Western world's will to assert itself... It is not only the trademark of Berlin, it is a symbol of freedom."

The groundbreaking for the chancellery, one of the few completely new buildings being constructed to house the administration, marked a symbolic point-of-no-return for the government's move from the former western capital of Bonn.

Parliament voted in 1991 to move to Berlin but planning feuds brought long delays. Renovation work is now underway in the former East German ministry buildings which will house their all-German equivalents from 1999.

Not wanting to hold up the move, Kohl has agreed the State Council Building -- former seat of East Germany's collective presidency under Erich Honecker -- should be used as a temporary chancellery if the new building is not ready on time.
The new chancellery, which will be ecologically correct with solar panels to generate some of its energy, will have 310 offices and 13 winter gardens.
Only a short stroll away from the Reichstag, which is being completely renovated inside, will stand one of three new office complexes for parliamentarians.
The upper house of parliament will move into the Prussian Landtag, a classical building just off the central Potsdamer Platz square that was split by the Berlin Wall.
